feature: 256-KiB HTTP/2 SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE for large single-stream messages

candidate.design: Both netz endpoints advertise a 256-KiB SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE so a 256-KiB message can fit in one DATA frame and take the direct decoder path instead of cross-DATA reassembly.

benchmark_method.schedule: three ABBA rounds; default, candidate, candidate, default
benchmark_method.host: shared host with unrelated load; no CPU pinning
benchmark_method.metric: ns_per_roundtrip from the benchmark result record

small_message_control.conclusion: 0/512/4-KiB persistent and per-call workloads stayed within about 0.7% of the 16-KiB default.

conclusion: A 256-KiB frame size makes a 256-KiB message fit one DATA frame and improves the persistent large-message workload by about 14.4% with no small-message regression. The library keeps the 16-KiB default because larger frames can increase multiplexing latency; large single-stream applications should opt in on both endpoints through Limits.max_frame_size.
